#### `feature_to_snap` {#feature_to_snap}

<p class="fl-facts">required · feature identifier · edited on the connection, not in the form</p>

**The feature placed at the surface the scan found.**

A `namespace:id` that some file in the pack defines. It is placed at the snapped position, not at this feature's own origin, and the name is looked up only once a surface has been found -- so a file naming a feature nothing defines reports that on the runs where the scan worked, and reports the scan's own failure on the runs where it did not.

#### `search_range` {#search_range}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · from format_version 1.26.50 · was `vertical_search_range`</p>

**How many blocks the scan may travel looking for a surface.**

Counted in blocks from the starting position along the chosen direction. The scan gives up once it has gone this far and the feature then places nothing.

The scan reaches a surface at exactly this many blocks; a range below 2 checks the block NEXT TO the origin rather than the origin itself.

#### `vertical_search_range` {#vertical_search_range}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · dropped at format_version 1.26.50 · renamed to `search_range`</p>

**How many blocks the scan may travel looking for a surface (the pre-1.26.50 spelling).**

The same setting as `search_range`; only the key name differs by version.

Renamed to `search_range` at format_version 1.26.50. Both spellings set the same value, so it is one key with two names -- and no version accepts both.

#### `surface` {#surface}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: floor · `wall` is new in game build 1.26.50.24</p>

**Which surface the scan is looking for.**

This picks the direction the scan walks as well as which side of the surface the feature ends up on. `random_horizontal` is the odd one -- see its own description.

The default is FLOOR, not ceiling -- this tool said ceiling until 2026-08-15 and was wrong about it in every build. `wall` tries the four horizontal directions in a random order.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `floor` — Walk downward and place on top of the first surface found. This is the default when the key is absent. A start that is already buried walks the other way instead, out of the solid, and lands on the same surface from underneath.
- `ceiling` — Walk upward and place underneath the first surface found. The mirror of floor, and what hanging features want.
- `wall` — Try the four horizontal directions in a random order and take the first that works. New in game version 1.26.50. Unlike floor and ceiling it costs random draws, because the order is shuffled.
- `random_horizontal` — Take one random draw and use it to pick FLOOR or CEILING. Despite the name, nothing horizontal happens: the result is always a floor snap or a ceiling snap, one or the other, decided per placement. If you want the four side directions, that is `wall`.

#### `allowed_surface_blocks` {#allowed_surface_blocks}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · blockList</p>

**Restricts which blocks count as the surface to snap to.**

Leave it out to accept any block that can genuinely support something on the face the scan arrived at.

With no allow-list the surface test is the real per-face one: the game asks whether the candidate can support something on the face the scan arrived at, which is not the same as asking whether it is solid. A {"tags": ...} entry matches NOTHING in the real game -- the preview will look like it works and the feature will place nothing in the world.

#### `allow_air_placement` {#allow_air_placement}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean</p>

**Whether the scan may start from a position that is open air.**

On by default when the key is absent. Turning it off makes a scan that begins in the open fail at once, before it takes a single step.

#### `allow_underwater_placement` {#allow_underwater_placement}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean</p>

**Whether water counts as open space the scan may pass through.**

Off by default. It means WATER specifically -- lava is never passable to this scan, whatever this is set to.

#### `embed_in_surface` {#embed_in_surface}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean</p>

**Places into the surface block itself instead of the open cell beside it.**

Off by default, which leaves the feature sitting on the surface rather than sunk into it.

#### `allow_non_air_placement` {#allow_non_air_placement}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean · absent: false · game build 1.26.50.24 -- whether the schema gates this key on format_version was NOT established, so it is offered at every version rather than hidden below one</p>

Lets a snap that starts inside a solid block escape outwards instead of failing.
